definitions.def: to look at something carefully in order to find a particular thing
to find the exact position of something
the act of stopping a process or action from happening
lasting for a long time or happening again and again

grammar_choice.en_template: Think about a time {{1:when/which}} you {{2:were startled/were startling}}.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 당신이 깜짝 놀랐던 때를 떠올려 보라.
explain: 선행사 a time(시간) + 완전한 절 → 관계부사 when.
사람이 '놀람을 당하는' 수동 의미 → were startled.

grammar_choice.en_template: Did you come to a sudden stop, freeze all your movements, and hold your breath {{1:as/which}} you scanned the environment for a threat?
grammar_choice.ko_full: 당신은 위협을 찾아 주변을 살피면서 갑자기 멈추고, 모든 움직임을 얼어붙게 하고, 숨을 참았는가?

grammar_choice.en_template: All these responses {{1:maximize/maximizes}} our ability {{2:to avoid/avoiding}} detection, locate the source of possible danger, and prepare to fight or flee.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 이 모든 반응은 발각을 피하고, 가능한 위험의 근원을 찾아내고, 싸우거나 도망갈 준비를 하는 우리의 능력을 극대화한다.
explain: ability + to V — to부정사(to avoid/locate/prepare 병렬).

grammar_choice.en_template: As sophisticated as language has become, it is still the creation of sound {{1:that/what}} might {{2:give away/be given away}} our location to a potential predator.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 언어가 아무리 정교해졌다 하더라도, 그것은 여전히 잠재적 포식자에게 우리의 위치를 알려줄 수 있는 소리의 생성이다.
explain: 선행사 the creation of sound 수식 주격 관계대명사 that.
뒤에 목적어 our location 존재 → 능동 give away.

grammar_choice.en_template: Because of this, the freeze response {{1:results in/results from}} the inhibition of language in highly stressful and traumatic {{2:situations/situation}}.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 이 때문에, 얼어붙는 반응은 매우 스트레스가 크고 외상적인 상황에서 언어의 억제로 이어진다.

grammar_choice.en_template: Natural selection {{1:promoted/has promoted}} the evolution of language but {{2:conserved/conserving}} the freeze rule.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 자연선택은 언어의 진화를 촉진했지만 얼어붙는 규칙은 보존했다.
explain: but으로 뒤의 conserved와 병렬 → 과거시제 promoted.
promoted ~ but conserved ~ — 두 과거동사 대조 병렬.

grammar_choice.en_template: When the threat passes, we {{1:begin/beginning}} to relax and find our voices again, perhaps even {{2:to laugh/laughing}} at our own reactions.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 위협이 지나가면, 우리는 긴장을 풀기 시작하고 다시 목소리를 되찾으며, 어쩌면 자신의 반응에 웃기까지 한다.
explain: begin to relax/find/(to) laugh — to부정사 병렬.

grammar_choice.ko_full: 그러나 만약 우리가 결코 긴장을 풀 수 없다면 어떻게 될까?

grammar_choice.en_template: What if our experiences {{1:shape/shapes}} our brain {{2:to be/being}} in a constant state of fear?
grammar_choice.ko_full: 만약 우리의 경험이 우리의 뇌를 끊임없는 공포 상태에 있도록 형성한다면 어떻게 될까?
explain: shape A to be ~ — 'A가 ~한 상태가 되도록 형성하다'(to부정사 보어).

grammar_choice.en_template: This interference {{1:with/of}} the proper development and integration of neural networks {{2:can result/can be resulted}} in chronic stress and even mental illness.

jumble.answer: Think about a time when you were startled.
Did you come to a sudden stop, freeze all your movements, and hold your breath as you scanned the environment for a threat?
All these responses maximize our ability to avoid detection, locate the source of possible danger, and prepare to fight or flee.
As sophisticated as language has become, it is still the creation of sound that might give away our location to a potential predator.
Because of this, the freeze response results in the inhibition of language in highly stressful and traumatic situations.
Natural selection promoted the evolution of language but conserved the freeze rule.
When the threat passes, we begin to relax and find our voices again, perhaps even to laugh at our own reactions.
But what if we can never relax?
What if our experiences shape our brain to be in a constant state of fear?
This interference with the proper development and integration of neural networks can result in chronic stress and even mental illness.
